p: Kentish Town City Farm sits on a quiet corner near Gospel Oak, tucked between railway lines and housing, and that hidden-away feel is part of the fun. You turn a corner and suddenly there are animals, gardens and the earthy smell of a farmyard right in the middle of North London. It's run as a charity, with local volunteers and community groups playing a big role in keeping it going.

It's a brilliant shout for a short, sweet outing with little ones. Let them meet the animals, peek into the gardens, and chat to anyone working on site, as they're usually happy to share what's going on. Keep an eye out for events and activities in the school holidays, as city farms often lay on extras like craft sessions or seasonal celebrations. Bring hand wipes and wear shoes you don't mind getting a bit grubby.

Gospel Oak puts you right on the edge of Hampstead Heath, and the southern side of the heath has more to explore than just the view from the top. Parliament Hill Lido is a striking Art Deco open-air pool, unheated and bracing, for the brave in your group. Kenwood House, at the northern edge of the heath, is a grand house with an impressive art collection including works by Rembrandt and Vermeer, and free entry. Close by, Highgate Cemetery is a beautiful, atmospheric place with Victorian tombs and the grave of Karl Marx, perfect for curious older kids and history buffs. That's an amazing mix within a short walk.
